name: systemctl
description: Controls systemd: services (units), system state, targets, and timers — the central administration tool on modern Linux.

flags.description: Restart / make a running service re-read its config.
State, memory, PID, and the last log lines of a service.
Start at boot / no longer start at boot (does not start it now).
Combine: enable --now starts the service immediately AND at boot.
All installed unit files with their enable state.
Re-read unit files after editing them.

examples.explanation: Starts nginx right now. It does not enable it for future boots.
The modern idiom: enable at boot AND start immediately in one command.

examples.output:
● nginx.service - A high performance web server
   Active: active (running) since Sat 2025-01-12 08:00:11 UTC; 2h 14min ago
   Memory: 12.4M
   CGroup: /system.slice/nginx.service
examples.explanation: Green "active (running)" is healthy; "failed" or "activating (auto-restart)" needs journalctl -u nginx for details.
Full stop+start. Use reload instead when the service supports it — reload re-reads config without dropping connections.

examples.output:
UNIT            LOAD   ACTIVE SUB    DESCRIPTION
mariadb.service loaded failed failed MariaDB 10.11 database server
examples.explanation: Lists all failed services — the first thing to check on a misbehaving server.
Required after editing any .service file, before restarting it.

about: systemd boots the system and supervises services, sockets, timers, and mounts as "units". enable creates symlinks in /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/; start runs it now. The two are independent — a service can be enabled but stopped, or running but disabled.
mistakes: Using enable expecting the service to start now — use enable --now.
Forgetting daemon-reload after editing unit files.
warnings: systemctl reboot and systemctl poweroff work too — double-check the hostname before running them on remote servers.
distroNotes: systemd distributions (Debian 8+, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL 7+, Arch, openSUSE). Alpine and Void use OpenRC/runit instead.
